I1.quote: The performance of gas storage of the material is further evaluated using H2 adsorption volumetric method. From this study, it shows that GRHA 1:3 has the highest hydrogen adsorption capacity which is up to 974 mmol/g (1.95 wt %).

I2.quote: Thus, in this study, we demonstrate successful attempt in producing porous carbon material which is graphene derived from rice husk activated in H3PO4 in the absence of inert gas condition during carbonation process.

notes: Measured sorbents: GRHA 1:1, 1:3, 1:5 (H3PO4-activated rice husk ash carbon); H2 uptake measured in a custom-made static volumetric rig (main p. 3, 'Static adsorption test'), uptake-versus-time curves in Fig. 10 (main p. 8) and qe,exp in Table 4 (main p. 10). BET areas (N2, 77 K) in Table 1 are on the same three samples. I2: the paper calls the material porous carbon / graphene-like; it reports no elemental or ash (silica) content, so carbon as the majority component by mass rests on the paper's own description. I3: 25 C and 30 bar are stated in Table 3; the method says H2 'is set at pressure 30 bar' in the loading column before expansion into the adsorption column, so 30 bar may be the charging rather than the equilibrium pressure (extraction issue, not eligibility). Unit inconsistency for extraction: '974 mmol/g (1.95 wt %)', '341.59 mmol/g (0.68 wt %)', '252.31 mmol/g (0.50 wt %)'; 1.95 wt% corresponds to about 9.7 mmol/g, not 974 mmol/g (Fig. 10 axis 'Amount of H2 adsorbed (mmol/g)', 0-1000). si1 is a Turnitin originality report containing the manuscript text; it is not a statement that the uptake values were published before, so duplicate_data does not apply. Not a review; is_retracted false and no retraction notice in the PDF.
